But the claim that it is undocumented is wrong. The change's own design.md, decision 6 (line 31), says the port uses `text-decoration-line`, `text-decoration-thickness` and `text-underline-offset`, and that the computed paint matches the design. The offsets are therefore a recorded, intentional decision in the OpenSpec change. They are pure cosmetic values with no requirement to contradict, and the spec does not forbid them. The finding is also minor and its own suggestion is optional, so no real defect remains.

The two declarations exist at src/ui/style.css:336 and :395, but the finding calls them "undocumented", and that is wrong. openspec/changes/update-page-palette/design.md, decision 6, says the port uses `text-decoration-line`, `text-decoration-thickness` and `text-underline-offset`, and that the computed paint matches the design. The extra property is therefore a recorded, intentional choice, not unexplained drift. The spec requirements mention only the line and thickness longhands, but the spec does not forbid the offset. There is also no user-visible or attacker-reachable defect: it is a cosmetic property that matches the design, and the only gap is that one spec sentence is silent about it.
